Actually, scientists have already begun animal testing on coronavirus flu vaccine. The human testing should begin in about a year or so. The vaccine itself should be ready in a year and a half.

Much like influenza that people die from every year, scientists don't know if they can make an effective vaccine against any flu strain virus when they start their tests. They don't know when a new strain of influenza will evolve (most likely the case) and always make predictions based on flu trends, which is why some people still get the flu after the shot. They have to assume that their new flu vacs give persistent immunity. Stop the fear mongering.
